guide.subject: 📮 How to send letters to {nick}
guide.intro:
Email your letters to {pet} at: {address}
{pet} will put each one in the Letters box for {nick} and hand it to her.
guide.format: The email subject becomes the letter's title, and the email body becomes the letter.
guide.date:
Want her to open a letter only on a certain day? There are two ways:
· Start the subject with the date, e.g. “[{date}] Happy birthday”
· Make the first line of the body “Open on: {date}”
Write the full year, month and day. Letters without a date can be opened as soon as she gets them.
guide.secret: Don't forget to put the secret word “{secret}” in the subject or body. {pet} won't accept letters without it.
guide.receipt: Once {pet} gets a letter, you'll get a confirmation email.

error.notReady: Email isn't set up yet: enter the pet's email address and app password
error.unknownServer: This email address wasn't recognized: pick your email provider from the list, or choose “Other email” and enter the incoming and outgoing servers yourself

error.tls: Secure connection error: check the server, port and SSL settings. The server's certificate may also be the problem

error.noAllow: His email (the address allowed to send letters) isn't filled in yet
error.tooSoon: He was just told a moment ago. Try again in a minute
error.pushUrl: The push URL isn't valid. It must start with http:// or https://
error.noSecret: A letter didn't include the secret word, so it wasn't put in the Letters box
error.emptyBody: “{title}” has an empty body, so it wasn't put in the Letters box

error.msAuth: Microsoft refused the sign-in: make sure you signed in with the Microsoft account for the email entered here, and that the registered app has IMAP and SMTP permissions
error.msNoClientId: Outlook mail needs a Microsoft account sign-in: first enter the application (client) ID you registered with Microsoft

139.name: 139 Mail
139.help: In 139 Mail on the web, turn on IMAP/SMTP under “Settings → Client settings”, then follow the steps to get an app password and enter it here.

auto.name: Detect automatically
auto.help: The servers are picked from the email address. Business email on a company domain can't be detected, so pick your provider from the list.

qq.name: QQ Mail
qq.help: In QQ Mail on the web, turn on “IMAP/SMTP service” under “Settings → Account”, generate an app password as prompted, and enter it here (not your QQ password).

exmail.name: Tencent Exmail
exmail.help: In Tencent Exmail on the web, turn on IMAP/SMTP under “Settings → Client settings”. If secure login is on, generate a client-specific password and enter it here.

netease.name: NetEase Mail (163, 126, yeah.net, 188)
netease.help: In NetEase Mail on the web, turn on IMAP/SMTP under “Settings → POP3/SMTP/IMAP”, generate an app password as prompted, and enter it here (not your email login password).

qiye163.name: NetEase Business Mail
qiye163.help: In NetEase Business Mail on the web, turn on IMAP/SMTP under “Settings → Client settings”. If client authorization passwords are on, enter that password here.

gmail.name: Gmail
gmail.help: Turn on 2-Step Verification in your Google Account first, then generate a 16-character password under “Security → App passwords” and enter it here (not your Google Account password).

outlook.name: Outlook / Hotmail / Microsoft 365
outlook.help: Microsoft email needs a Microsoft account sign-in: enter the application ID, click “Sign in with Microsoft”, open the Microsoft page in your browser, enter the code shown and approve. Work or school Microsoft 365 email also uses this option.
outlook.register: To register an application ID: sign in to the Azure portal (portal.azure.com) with your Microsoft account and open “App registrations → New registration”. Any name works. For supported account types, choose “Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts”. After registering, turn on “Allow public client flows” under “Authentication”, and add IMAP.AccessAsUser.All and SMTP.Send under “API permissions”. Finally, enter the “Application (client) ID” from the Overview page here.

icloud.name: iCloud Mail
icloud.help: Turn on two-factor authentication for your Apple Account first, then generate a password under “App-Specific Passwords” at account.apple.com and enter it here.

yahoo.name: Yahoo Mail
yahoo.help: Generate an “app password” under “Account security” in your Yahoo account and enter it here.

sina.name: Sina Mail
sina.help: In Sina Mail on the web, turn on the service under “Settings → Client POP/IMAP/SMTP”, then follow the steps to get an app password and enter it here.

sohu.name: Sohu Mail
sohu.help: In Sohu Mail on the web, turn on the service under “Settings → POP3/SMTP/IMAP”, set a separate password and enter it here.

aliyun.name: Alibaba Mail
aliyun.help: In Alibaba Mail on the web, turn on IMAP/SMTP in the settings and enter your email password here. If secure login is on, enter the third-party client security password instead.

custom.name: Other email (enter servers yourself)
custom.help: Enter the incoming (IMAP) and outgoing (SMTP) servers, ports and encryption from your email provider below. You can usually find them in your provider's web mail help.
